BitField.description: Specifies the match contribution condition for bit slice 0.
BitField.name: CFG0

Enum.description: Sticky rising edge. Match occurs if a rising edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.
Enum.name: STICKY_RISING_EDGE

Enum.description: Sticky falling edge. Match occurs if a falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.
Enum.name: STICKY_FALLING_EDGE

Enum.description: Sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs if either a rising or falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.
Enum.name: STICKY_RISING_FALLING_EDGE

Enum.description: High level. Match (for this bit slice) occurs when there is a high level on the input specified for this bit slice in the PMSRC register.
Enum.name: HIGH_LEVEL

Enum.description: Low level. Match occurs when there is a low level on the specified input.
Enum.name: LOW_LEVEL

Enum.description: Constant 0. This bit slice never contributes to a match (should be used to disable any unused bit slices).
Enum.name: CONSTANT_ZERO

Enum.description: Event. Non-sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs on an event when either a rising or falling edge is first detected on the specified input (this is a non-sticky version of value 0x3). This bit is cleared after 1 clock cycle.
Enum.name: EVENT

Enum.description: Sticky falling edge. Match occurs if a falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.
Enum.name: STICKY_FALLING_EDGE

Enum.description: Sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs if either a rising or falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.
Enum.name: STICKY_RISING_FALLING_EDGE

Enum.description: High level. Match (for this bit slice) occurs when there is a high level on the input specified for this bit slice in the PMSRC register.
Enum.name: HIGH_LEVEL

Enum.description: Low level. Match occurs when there is a low level on the specified input.
Enum.name: LOW_LEVEL

Enum.description: Constant 0. This bit slice never contributes to a match (should be used to disable any unused bit slices).
Enum.name: CONSTANT_ZERO

Enum.description: Event. Non-sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs on an event when either a rising or falling edge is first detected on the specified input (this is a non-sticky version of value 0x3). This bit is cleared after 1 clock cycle.
Enum.name: EVENT

BitField.description: Monitors the interrupt flag. Writing 0 indicates no pending interrupt or no operation. Writing 1 indicates pending interrupt, because TIMERn has reached the end of the time interval. If CTRLn[INTEN] in the CONTROLn also gets 1, then the interrupt for timer channel n and the global interrupt are generated. Writing 1 to this field bit clears the interrupt request.
BitField.name: INTFLAG

Enum.description: This timer channel is not in use.
Enum.name: NO

Enum.description: This timer channel is in use.
Enum.name: YES

Enum.description: Process complete. Measurement cycle is complete. The results are ready in the RESULT field.
Enum.name: CYCLE_DONE

Enum.description: In Progress. Measurement cycle is in progress.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Frequency Measurement Mode. FREQMECTRL works in a Frequency Measurement mode. Once the measurement starts (real count start is aligned at rising edge arrival on reference clock), the target counter increments by the target clock until the reference counter running by the reference clock reaches the count end point selected by REF_SCALE.
Enum.name: FREQ_ME_MODE

Enum.description: Pulse Width Measurement mode. FREQMECTRL works in a Pulse Width Measurement mode, measuring the high or low period of reference clock input selected by PULSE_POL. The target counter starts incrementing by the target clock once a corresponding trigger edge (rising edge for high period measurement and falling edge for low period) occurs.
Enum.name: PULSE_ME_MODE

Enum.description: High Period. High period of reference clock is measured in Pulse Width Measurement mode triggered by the rising edge on the reference clock input.
Enum.name: HIGH_PERIOD

Enum.description: Low Period. Low period of reference clock is measured in Pulse Width Measurement mode triggered by the falling edge on the reference clock input.
Enum.name: LOW_PERIOD

Enum.description: Not in reset. The RTC is not held in reset. Clear SWRESET before configuring or initiating any operation of the RTC.
Enum.name: NOT_IN_RESET

BitField.description: RTC 1 Hz Timer Alarm Flag Status
BitField.name: ALARM1HZ

Enum.description: No match. No match condition has occurred on the 1 Hz RTC timer. Writing a 0 has no effect.
Enum.name: NO_MATCH

BitField.description: RTC 1 kHz Timer Wake-up Flag Status
BitField.name: WAKE1KHZ

Enum.description: Run. The RTC 1 kHz timer is running. Writing a 0 has no effect.
Enum.name: RUN

Enum.description: Time-out. The 1 kHz high-resolution/wake-up timer has timed out. This flag generates an RTC wake-up interrupt request RTC-WAKE which can also wake up the device from any low power mode. Write 1 to clear.
Enum.name: TIME_OUT

BitField.description: RTC 1 Hz Timer Alarm Enable for Deep Power-down
BitField.name: ALARMDPD_EN

Enum.description: Disable. A match on the 1 Hz RTC timer does not bring the device out of Deep Power-down mode.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Enable. A match on the 1 Hz RTC timer brings the device out of Deep Power-down mode.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: RTC 1 kHz Timer Wake-up Enable for Deep Power-down
BitField.name: WAKEDPD_EN

Enum.description: Disable. A match on the 1 kHz RTC timer does not bring the device out of Deep Power-down mode.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Enable. A match on the 1 kHz RTC timer brings the device out of Deep Power-down mode.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Disable. A match on the 1 kHz RTC timer does not bring the device out of Deep Power-down mode.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Enable. The 1 kHz RTC timer is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Disable. The RTC 1 Hz and 1 kHz clocks are shut down and the RTC operation is disabled. RTC_EN should be 0 when writing to load a value in the RTC counter (COUNT) register .
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Enable. The 1 Hz RTC clock is running and RTC operation is enabled. The first clock to the RTC counter occurs 1 s after RTC_EN is set. To also enable the high-resolution, 1 kHz clock, set CTRL[RTC1KHZ_EN] = 1.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Enable. The RTC oscillator is enabled. RTC_OSC_PD must be cleared for the RTC module to function.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Shut Off. The RTC operation is disabled. The RTC oscillator is shut-off to limit power consumption.
Enum.name: SHUT_OFF

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.
Enum.name: NOT_IDLE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.
Enum.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Disabled. The MstPending interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MstPending interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The MstArbLoss interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MstArbLoss interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The MstStStpErr interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MstStStpErr interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The SlvPending interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The SlvPending interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The SlvNotStr interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The SlvNotStr interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The SlvDeSel interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The SlvDeSel interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The MonRdy interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MonRdy interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The MonOv interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MonOv interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The MonIdle interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MonIdle interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Event time-out interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Event time-out interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The SCL time-out interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The SCL time-out interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MSTPENDING

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MSTARBLOSS

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MSTSTSTPERR

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_SLVPENDING

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_SLVNOTSTR

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_SLVDESEL

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MONRDY

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MONOV

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MONIDLE

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_EVENTTIMEOUT

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_SCLTIMEOUT

BitField.description: Time-out time value, the bottom 4 bits
BitField.name: TOMIN

Enum.description: A time-out will occur after 16 counts of the I2C function clock.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT16

Enum.description: A time-out will occur after 32 counts of the I2C function clock.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT32

Enum.description: A time-out will occur after 65,536 counts of the I2C function clock.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT65K

Enum.description: FCLK is used directly by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKUNDIVIDED

Enum.description: FCLK is divided by 2 before being used by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKDIV2

Enum.description: FCLK is divided by 3 before being used by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKDIV3

Enum.description: FCLK is divided by 65,536 before being used by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKDIV65K

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Master function to continue to the next operation. This action must done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: Start. A Start will be generated on the I2C bus at the next allowed time.
Enum.name: START

Enum.description: Stop. A Stop will be generated on the I2C bus at the next allowed time, preceded by a NACK to the slave if the master is receiving data from the slave (in Master Receiver mode).
Enum.name: STOP

Enum.description: Disable. No DMA requests are generated for master operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enable. A DMA request is generated for I2C master data operations. When this I2C master is generating Acknowledge bits in Master Receiver mode, the acknowledge is generated automatically.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: 2 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 2 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_2CLOCKS

Enum.description: 3 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 3 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_3CLOCKS

Enum.description: 4 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 4 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_4CLOCKS

Enum.description: 5 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 5 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_5CLOCKS

Enum.description: 6 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 6 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_6CLOCKS

Enum.description: 7 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 7 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_7CLOCKS

Enum.description: 8 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 8 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_8CLOCKS

Enum.description: 9 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 9 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_9CLOCKS

Enum.description: 2 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 2 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_2CLOCKS

Enum.description: 3 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 3 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider .
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_3CLOCKS

Enum.description: 4 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 4 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_4CLOCKS

Enum.description: 5 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 5 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_5CLOCKS

Enum.description: 6 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 6 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_6CLOCKS

Enum.description: 7 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 7 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_7CLOCKS

Enum.description: 8 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 8 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_8CLOCKS

Enum.description: 9 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 9 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_9CLOCKS

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.
Enum.name: I2C_READ

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Mask. The SLVQUAL0 field is used as a logical mask for matching address 0.
Enum.name: MASK

Enum.description: Extend. The SLVQUAL0 field is used to extend address 0 matching in a range of addresses.
Enum.name: EXTEND

Enum.description: No start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NO_START_DETECTED

Enum.description: Start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: START_DETECTED

Enum.description: No repeated start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NOT_DETECTED

Enum.description: Repeated start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: DETECTED

Enum.description: Acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was acknowledged by at least one master or slave receiver.
Enum.name: ACKNOWLEDGED

Enum.description: Not acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was not acknowledged by any receiver.
Enum.name: NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED

BitField.description: Module identifier for the selected function
BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.
Enum.name: I2C_READ

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.

Enum.name: NORMAL

BitField.description: Module identifier for the selected function
BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.
Enum.name: NOT_IDLE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.
Enum.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT

Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.
Enum.name: I2C_READ

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.name: MASK

Enum.description: Extend. The SLVQUAL0 field is used to extend address 0 matching in a range of addresses.

Enum.description: No start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NO_START_DETECTED

Enum.description: Start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: START_DETECTED

Enum.description: No repeated start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NOT_DETECTED

Enum.description: Repeated start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: DETECTED

Enum.description: Acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was acknowledged by at least one master or slave receiver.
Enum.name: ACKNOWLEDGED

Enum.description: Not acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was not acknowledged by any receiver.
Enum.name: NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED

BitField.description: Module identifier for the selected function
BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.

BitField.description: Module identifier for the selected function
BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.
Enum.name: NOT_IDLE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.
Enum.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT

SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.
Enum.name: I2C_READ

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: No start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NO_START_DETECTED

Enum.description: Start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: START_DETECTED

Enum.description: No repeated start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NOT_DETECTED

Enum.description: Repeated start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: DETECTED

Enum.description: Acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was acknowledged by at least one master or slave receiver.
Enum.name: ACKNOWLEDGED

Enum.description: Not acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was not acknowledged by any receiver.
Enum.name: NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED

BitField.description: Module identifier for the selected function
BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.
Enum.name: NOT_IDLE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.
Enum.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Disabled. The MstPending interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MstPending interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.
Enum.name: NOT_IDLE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.
Enum.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Disabled. The MstPending interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MstPending interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MonRdy interrupt is enabled.

Enum.description: Disabled. The MonOv interrupt is disabled.

Enum.description: Enabled. The MonOv interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The MonIdle interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The MonIdle interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Event time-out interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Event time-out interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The SCL time-out interrupt is disabled.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The SCL time-out interrupt is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.name: CLEAR_MSTPENDING

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MSTARBLOSS

Enum.description: Clears the interrupt bit in INTENSET register
Enum.name: CLEAR_MSTSTSTPERR

Enum.name: CLEAR_SLVPENDING

BitField.name: TOMIN

Enum.description: A time-out will occur after 16 counts of the I2C function clock.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT16

Enum.description: A time-out will occur after 32 counts of the I2C function clock.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT32

Enum.description: A time-out will occur after 65,536 counts of the I2C function clock.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT65K

Enum.description: FCLK is used directly by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKUNDIVIDED

Enum.description: FCLK is divided by 2 before being used by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKDIV2

Enum.description: FCLK is divided by 3 before being used by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKDIV3

Enum.description: FCLK is divided by 65,536 before being used by the I2C.
Enum.name: FCLKDIV65K

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Master function to continue to the next operation. This action must done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: Start. A Start will be generated on the I2C bus at the next allowed time.
Enum.name: START

Enum.description: Stop. A Stop will be generated on the I2C bus at the next allowed time, preceded by a NACK to the slave if the master is receiving data from the slave (in Master Receiver mode).
Enum.name: STOP

Enum.description: Disable. No DMA requests are generated for master operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enable. A DMA request is generated for I2C master data operations. When this I2C master is generating Acknowledge bits in Master Receiver mode, the acknowledge is generated automatically.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: 2 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 2 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_2CLOCKS

Enum.description: 3 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 3 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_3CLOCKS

Enum.description: 4 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 4 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_4CLOCKS

Enum.description: 5 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 5 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_5CLOCKS

Enum.description: 6 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 6 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_6CLOCKS

Enum.description: 7 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 7 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_7CLOCKS

Enum.description: 8 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 8 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_8CLOCKS

Enum.description: 9 clocks. Minimum SCL low time is 9 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLLOW_9CLOCKS

Enum.description: 2 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 2 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_2CLOCKS

Enum.description: 3 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 3 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider .
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_3CLOCKS

Enum.description: 4 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 4 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_4CLOCKS

Enum.description: 5 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 5 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_5CLOCKS

Enum.description: 6 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 6 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_6CLOCKS

Enum.description: 7 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 7 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.
Enum.name: MSTSCLHIGH_7CLOCKS

Enum.description: 8 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 8 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.

Enum.description: 9 clocks. Minimum SCL high time is 9 clocks of the I2C clock pre-divider.

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.
Enum.name: I2C_READ

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
