Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Mask. The SLVQUAL0 field is used as a logical mask for matching address 0.
Enum.name: MASK

Enum.description: Extend. The SLVQUAL0 field is used to extend address 0 matching in a range of addresses.
Enum.name: EXTEND

Enum.description: No start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NO_START_DETECTED

Enum.description: Start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: START_DETECTED

Enum.description: No repeated start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NOT_DETECTED

Enum.description: Repeated start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: DETECTED

Enum.description: Acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was acknowledged by at least one master or slave receiver.
Enum.name: ACKNOWLEDGED

Enum.description: Not acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was not acknowledged by any receiver.
Enum.name: NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.

Enum.name: DETECTED

Enum.name: NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED

BitField.description: Module identifier for the selected function
BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.
Enum.name: NOT_IDLE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.
Enum.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.
Enum.name: TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.
Enum.name: CONTINUE

Enum.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: NACK

Enum.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.
Enum.name: I2C_WRITE

Enum.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.
Enum.name: I2C_READ

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.
Enum.name: NORMAL

Enum.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC

Enum.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.

Enum.description: No start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: NO_START_DETECTED

Enum.description: Start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: START_DETECTED

Enum.name: NOT_DETECTED

Enum.description: Repeated start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.
Enum.name: DETECTED

Enum.description: Not acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was not acknowledged by any receiver.

BitField.description: Module identifier for the selected function
BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).

Enum.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.
Enum.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK

BitField.name: ID

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: RECEIVE_READY

Enum.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.
Enum.name: TRANSMIT_READY

Enum.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.
Enum.name: NACK_DATA

Enum.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).
Enum.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS

Enum.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.
Enum.name: IN_PROGRESS

Enum.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).
Enum.name: PENDING

Enum.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.
Enum.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS

Enum.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE

Enum.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).
Enum.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT

Enum.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.
Enum.name: STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.
Enum.name: NOT_STRETCHING

Enum.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.
Enum.name: NOT_SELECTED

Enum.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.
Enum.name: SELECTED

Enum.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.
Enum.name: NOT_DESELECTED

Enum.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.
Enum.name: DESELECTED

Enum.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.
Enum.name: NO_DATA

Enum.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.
Enum.name: DATA_WAITING

Enum.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.
Enum.name: NO_OVERRUN

Enum.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.
Enum.name: OVERRUN

Enum.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.
Enum.name: INACTIVE

Enum.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.
Enum.name: ACTIVE

Enum.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.
Enum.name: NOT_IDLE

Enum.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.
Enum.name: IDLE

Enum.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.

Enum.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.
Enum.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.
Enum.name: NO_TIMEOUT

Enum.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.

Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: Enabled. The SPI is enabled for operation.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.name: SLAVE_MODE

Enum.description: Master mode. The SPI will operate in master mode. SCK, MOSI, and the SSEL signals are outputs; MISO is an input.
Enum.name: MASTER_MODE

Enum.description: Standard. Data is transmitted and received in standard MSB-first order.
Enum.name: STANDARD

Enum.description: Reverse. Data is transmitted and received in reverse order (LSB first).
Enum.name: REVERSE

Enum.name: LOW

Enum.description: High. The rest state of the clock (between transfers) is high.
Enum.name: HIGH

Enum.description: High. The SSEL0 pin is active high.
Enum.name: HIGH

Enum.description: Low. The SSEL1 pin is active low.
Enum.name: LOW

Enum.description: High. The SSEL1 pin is active high.
Enum.name: HIGH

Enum.description: Low. The SSEL2 pin is active low.
Enum.name: LOW

Enum.description: High. The SSEL2 pin is active high.
Enum.name: HIGH

Enum.description: Low. The SSEL3 pin is active low.
Enum.name: LOW

Enum.description: High. The SSEL3 pin is active high.
Enum.name: HIGH

Enum.name: TRANSFER_DELAY2

Enum.description: A transmit FIFO error has not occurred.

Enum.name: TXERR

Enum.description: A receive FIFO overflow has not occurred
Enum.name: NO_RXERR

Enum.description: A receive FIFO overflow has occurred, caused by software or DMA not emptying the FIFO fast enough
Enum.name: RXERR

Enum.description: The peripheral function has not asserted an interrupt
Enum.name: NO_PERINT

Enum.name: PERINT

Enum.name: TXFIFO_ISFULL

Enum.name: TXFIFO_ISNOTFULL

Enum.name: RXFIFO_ISNOTEMPTY

Enum.description: The receive FIFO is not full
Enum.name: RXFIFO_ISNOTFULL

Enum.description: SSEL is not deasserted. This piece of data is not treated as the end of a transfer. SSEL will not be deasserted at the end of this data.
Enum.name: NOT_DEASSERTED

Enum.description: SSEL is deasserted. This piece of data is treated as the end of a transfer. SSEL will be deasserted at the end of this piece of data.
Enum.name: DEASSERTED

Enum.description: Data not EOF. This piece of data transmitted is not treated as the end of a frame.
Enum.name: NOT_EOF

Enum.description: Data EOF. This piece of data is treated as the end of a frame, causing the Frame_delay time to be inserted before subsequent data is transmitted.
Enum.name: EOF

Enum.description: Read received data. Received data must be read, to allow transmission to proceed. SPI transmit will halt when the receive data FIFO is full. In slave mode, an overrun error will occur if received data is not read before new data is received.
Enum.name: READ

Enum.description: Ignore received data. Received data is ignored, allowing transmission without reading unneeded received data. No receiver flags are generated.
Enum.name: IGNORE

Enum.description: Data transfer is 4 bits in length
Enum.name: LEN_4BITS

Enum.description: Data transfer is 5 bits in length
Enum.name: LEN_5BITS

Enum.description: Data transfer is 16 bits in length
Enum.name: LEN_16BITS

Enum.description: This is not the 1st data after the SSELs went from deasserted to asserted
Enum.name: SOT0

Enum.description: This is the 1st data after the SSELs went from deasserted to asserted (i.e., any previous transfer has ended). This information can be used to identify the 1st piece of data in cases where the transfer length is greater than 16 bits.
Enum.name: SOT1

Enum.name: EOF

Enum.description: Read received data. Received data must be read, to allow transmission to proceed. SPI transmit will halt when the receive data FIFO is full. In slave mode, an overrun error will occur if received data is not read before new data is received.

Enum.name: LEN_5BITS

Enum.name: SOT0

Enum.name: RXFIFO_ISNOTEMPTY

Enum.description: Trigger when the RX FIFO has received 2 entries
Enum.name: RXLVL2

Enum.description: Trigger when the RX FIFO has received 16 entries (has become full)
Enum.name: RXLVL15

Enum.description: No interrupt will be generated for a transmit error.
Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: An interrupt will be generated when a transmit error occurs.

Enum.name: DISABLED

Enum.description: An interrupt will be generated when a receive error occurs.

BitField.name: RESET

BitField.name: CRC_VALUE

BitField.name: SEC

BitField.name: DED

BitField.name: LOCKED

BitField.description: OTP PROGFAIL status. Write 1 to clear.
BitField.name: PROGFAIL

BitField.description: OTP Power OK status. Indicate that power VDD are in the operating range.
BitField.name: PWOK

BitField.name: SEC_RELOAD

BitField.description: OTP Double Error Detect status of ECC during reload process. Write 1 to clear.
BitField.name: DED_RELOAD

BitField.description: CRC failed when set by hardware for CRC operation. Write 1 to clear.
BitField.name: CRC_FAIL

BitField.description: Indicate all shadows registers have been loaded with their corresponding fuse words when set by the controller after reset.
BitField.name: FUSE_LATCHED

BitField.description: Sample Clock source selection for Flash Reading
BitField.name: RXCLKSRC

Enum.description: Dummy Read strobe generated by FlexSPI Controller and loopback internally.
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: Dummy Read strobe generated by FlexSPI Controller and loopback from DQS pad.
Enum.name: val1

Enum.description: Flash provided Read strobe and input from DQS pad
Enum.name: val3

BitField.description: Half Speed Serial Flash Access Enable.
BitField.name: HSEN

Enum.description: Disable divide by 2 of serial flash clock for half clock frequency.
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: Enable divide by 2 of serial flash clock for half clock frequency.
Enum.name: val1

Enum.description: Doze mode support disabled. AHB clock and serial clock will not be gated off when there is doze mode request from system.
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: Doze mode support enabled. AHB clock and serial clock will be gated off when there is doze mode request from system.
Enum.name: val1

BitField.description: This bit is used to enable SCLK output free-running. For FPGA applications, the external device may use SCLK as reference clock to its internal PLL.
BitField.name: SCKFREERUNEN

BitField.description: This bit is used to enable/disable the data learning feature.
BitField.name: LEARNEN

BitField.description: Timeout wait cycle for IP command grant.
BitField.name: IPGRANTWAIT

BitField.description: Timeout wait cycle for AHB command grant.
BitField.name: AHBGRANTWAIT

BitField.description: Command Sequence Execution will timeout and abort after SEQWAIT * 1024 Serial Root Clock cycles. When sequence execution timeout occurs, there will be an interrupt generated (INTR[SEQTIMEOUT]) if this interrupt is enabled (INTEN[SEQTIMEOUTEN] is set 0x1) and AHB command is ignored by arbitrator.
BitField.name: SEQWAIT

Enum.description: AHB RX/TX Buffer will not be cleared automatically when FlexSPI returns Stop mode ACK.
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: AHB RX/TX Buffer will be cleared automatically when FlexSPI returns Stop mode ACK.
Enum.name: val1

BitField.description: The sampling clock phase selection will be reset to phase 0 when this bit is written with 0x1. This bit will be auto-cleared immediately.
BitField.name: CLRLEARNPHASE

Enum.description: The sampling clock phase selection will be reset to phase 0 when this bit is written with 0x1. This bit will be auto-cleared immediately.
Enum.name: val1

BitField.description: All external devices are same devices (both in type and size) for A1/A2/B1/B2.
BitField.name: SAMEDEVICEEN

Enum.description: In Individual mode, FLSHA1CRx/FLSHA2CRx/FLSHB1CRx/FLSHB2CRx register setting will be applied to Flash A1/A2/B1/B2 separately. In Parallel mode, FLSHA1CRx register setting will be applied to Flash A1 and B1, FLSHA2CRx register setting will be applied to Flash A2 and B2. FLSHB1CRx/FLSHB2CRx register setting will be ignored.
Enum.name: individual_parallel

Enum.description: FLSHA1CR0/FLSHA1CR1/FLSHA1CR2 register setting will be applied to Flash A1/A2/B1/B2. FLSHA2CRx/FLSHB1CRx/FLSHB2CRx will be ignored.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Wait cycle (in AHB clock cycle) for idle state before suspended command sequence resumed.
BitField.name: RESUMEWAIT

BitField.description: Parallel mode enabled for AHB triggered Command (both read and write).
BitField.name: APAREN

Enum.description: Flash will be accessed in Individual mode.
Enum.name: individual

Enum.description: Flash will be accessed in Parallel mode.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Clear the status/pointers of AHB TX Buffer. Auto-cleared.
BitField.name: CLRAHBTXBUF

BitField.description: Enable AHB bus cachable read access support.
BitField.name: CACHABLEEN

Enum.description: Disabled. When there is AHB bus cachable read access, FlexSPI will not check whether it hit AHB TX Buffer.
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: Enabled. When there is AHB bus cachable read access, FlexSPI will check whether it hit AHB TX Buffer first.
Enum.name: val1

BitField.description: Enable AHB bus bufferable write access support.
BitField.name: BUFFERABLEEN

Enum.description: Disabled. For all AHB write accesses (bufferable or non-bufferable), FlexSPI will return AHB Bus ready after all data is transmitted to external device and AHB command finished.
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: Enabled. For AHB bufferable write access, FlexSPI will return AHB Bus ready when the AHB command is granted by arbitrator and will not wait for AHB command finished.
Enum.name: val1

BitField.description: AHB Read Address option bit. This option bit is intended to remove AHB burst start address alignment limitation.
BitField.name: READADDROPT

Enum.description: There is AHB read burst start address alignment limitation when flash is accessed in parallel mode or flash is word-addressable.
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: There is no AHB read burst start address alignment limitation. FlexSPI will fetch more data than AHB burst required to meet the alignment requirement.
Enum.name: val1

Enum.description: Suspended AHB read prefetch will start to resume when AHB is IDLE
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: Suspended AHB read prefetch will not resume once it is aborted
Enum.name: val1

Enum.description: AHB read size will be decided by other register setting like PREFETCH_EN,OTFAD_EN...
Enum.name: val0

Enum.description: AHB read size to up size to 8 bytes aligned, no prefetching
Enum.name: val1

BitField.description: For certain devices (such as FPGA), it need some time to write data into internal memory after the command sequences finished on FlexSPI interface. If another Read command sequence comes before previous programming finished internally, the read data may be wrong. This field is used to hold AHB Bus ready for AHB write access to wait the programming finished in external device. Then there will be no AHB read command triggered before the programming finished in external device. The Wait cycle between AHB triggered command sequences finished on FlexSPI interface and AHB return Bus ready: AWRWAIT * AWRWAITUNIT
BitField.name: AWRWAIT

BitField.description: This status bit indicates the state machine in ARB_CTL is busy and there is command sequence granted by arbitrator and not finished yet on FlexSPI interface. When ARB_CTL state (ARBIDLE=0x1) is idle, there will be no transaction on FlexSPI interface also (SEQIDLE=0x1). So this bit should be polled to wait for FlexSPI controller become idle instead of SEQIDLE.

Enum.description: Power-down the USB full-speed drivers. This turns off the current starvation sources and puts the drivers into high-impedance output
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Power down USB PHY current bias block.
BitField.name: TXPWDIBIAS

Enum.description: Power-down the USB PHY current bias block for the transmitter. This bit should be set only when the USB is in suspend mode. This effectively powers down the entire USB transmit path.
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Power down USB PHY V-I converter and current mirror.
BitField.name: TXPWDV2I

Enum.description: Power-down the USB PHY transmit V-to-I converter and the current mirror
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Power down USB HS receiver envelope detector.
BitField.name: RXPWDENV

Enum.description: Power down the USB high-speed receiver envelope detector (squelch signal)
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Power down USB FS differential receiver.
BitField.name: RXPWD1PT1

Enum.description: Power down the USB full-speed differential receiver
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Power down USB HS differential receiver.
BitField.name: RXPWDDIFF

Enum.description: Power down the USB high-speed differential receiver
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: Power down USB PHY receiver except the FS differential.
BitField.name: RXPWDRX

Enum.description: Power-down the entire USB PHY receiver block except for the full-speed differential receiver
Enum.name: ENABLE

BitField.description: For certain devices (such as FPGA), it need some time to write data into internal memory after the command sequences finished on FlexSPI interface. If another Read command sequence comes before previous programming finished internally, the read data may be wrong. This field is used to hold AHB Bus ready for AHB write access to wait the programming finished in external device. Then there will be no AHB read command triggered before the programming finished in external device. The Wait cycle between AHB triggered command sequences finished on FlexSPI interface and AHB return Bus ready: AWRWAIT * AWRWAITUNIT

Enum.description: When the device is not connected or not suspended, a writing a 0 has no effect. Writing a 1 never has an effect.
Enum.name: DSUS_0

Enum.description: It is set to 1 when the device has not seen any activity on its upstream port for more than 3 ms. It is reset to 0 on any activity. When the device is suspended (Suspend bit DSUS = 1) and the software writes a 0 to it, the device will generate a remote wake-up. This will only happen when the device is connected (Connect bit = 1).
Enum.name: DSUS_1

Enum.description: Software can only write a 0 to this bit when the LPM_REWP bit is set to 1. Hardware resets this bit when it receives a host initiated resume. Hardware only updates the LPM_SUS bit when the LPM_SUPP bit is equal to 1.
Enum.name: LPM_SUS_0

Enum.description: When the device is in the LPM suspended state (LPM suspend bit = 1) and the software writes a 0 to this bit, the device will generate a remote walk-up.
Enum.name: LPM_SUS_1

Enum.description: No Resume (K-state) detected or driven on the port.
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Resume (K-state) detected or driven on the port.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Enabled port is in the L1 or L2 suspend state
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Port is not in the reset state
Enum.name: DISABLE

Enum.description: Port is in the reset state
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Device was unable to enter the L1 state at this time (NYET)
Enum.name: ENABLE1

Enum.description: Device does not support the L1 state (STALL)

Enum.description: Timeout/Error - Device failed to respond or an error occurred.
Enum.name: ENABLE3

BitField.description: If this bit is set to one, the port will behave as a USB device. If this bit is set to zero, the port will be controlled by the USB host block.
BitField.name: DEV_ENABLE

Enum.description: Dual counter. The SCT operates as two 16-bit counters named COUNTER_L and COUNTER_H.
Enum.name: DUAL_COUNTER

Enum.description: Unified counter. The SCT operates as a unified 32-bit counter.
Enum.name: UNIFIED_COUNTER

Enum.description: System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the entire SCT module including all counters and counter prescalers.
Enum.name: SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE

Enum.description: Sampled System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the SCT module, but the counter and prescalers are only enabled to count when the designated edge is detected on the input selected by the CKSEL field. The minimum pulse width on the selected clock-gate input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the high-performance, sampled-clock mode.
Enum.name: SAMPLED_SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE

Enum.description: SCT Input Clock Mode. The input/edge selected by the CKSEL field clocks the SCT module, including all counters and prescalers, after first being synchronized to the system clock. The minimum pulse width on the clock input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the low-power, sampled-clock mode.
Enum.name: SCT_INPUT_CLOCK_MODE

Enum.description: Asynchronous Mode. The entire SCT module is clocked directly by the input/edge selected by the CKSEL field. In this mode, the SCT outputs are switched synchronously to the SCT input clock - not the system clock. The input clock rate must be at least half the system clock rate and can be the same or faster than the system clock.
Enum.name: ASYNCHRONOUS_MODE

BitField.description: SCT Clock Select. The specific functionality of the designated input/edge is dependent on the CLKMODE bit selection in this register.
BitField.name: CKSEL

Enum.description: No Reload. Prevents the lower match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers.
Enum.name: NO_RELOAD

Enum.description: No Reload. Prevents the higher match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers.
Enum.name: NO_RELOAD_H

Enum.description: Enable. A match on match register 0 is the LIMIT condition. No need to define an associated event.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.description: Enable. A match on match register 0 is the LIMIT condition. No need to define an associated event.
Enum.name: ENABLE

Enum.name: UP

Enum.description: Down. The L or unified counter is counting down.
Enum.name: DOWN

Enum.description: Up. The counter counts up to a limit condition, then is cleared to zero.
Enum.name: UP

Enum.description: Up-down. The counter counts up to a limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.
Enum.name: UP_DOWN

Enum.description: Up. The H counter is counting up.
Enum.name: UP

Enum.description: Down. The H counter is counting down.
Enum.name: DOWN

Enum.description: Up. The H counter counts up to its limit condition, then is cleared to zero.
Enum.name: UP

Enum.description: Up-down. The H counter counts up to its limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.
Enum.name: UP_DOWN

BitField.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_L] = 0 (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.
BitField.name: STARTMSK_L

BitField.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_H] = 0 (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.
BitField.name: STARTMSK_H

Enum.description: AES is enabled (see also CRYPTCFG register for more controls)
Enum.name: AES

Enum.description: ICB-AES is enabled (see also CRYPTCFG register for more controls)
Enum.name: ICB_AES

Enum.description: Starts a new Hash/Crypto and initializes the Digest/Result.
Enum.name: START

Enum.description: Allows the SHA RELOAD registers to be used.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: DMA is not used. Processor writes the necessary words when WAITING is set (interrupts), unless AHB Master is used.
Enum.name: NOT_USED

Enum.description: DMA will push in the data.
Enum.name: PUSH

Enum.description: DMA is not used. Processor reads the digest/output in response to DIGEST interrupt.
Enum.name: NOTUSED

Enum.description: Not waiting for data - may be disabled or may be busy. For cryptographic uses, this is not set if IsLast is set nor will it set until at least 1 word is read of the output.
Enum.name: NOT_WAITING

Enum.description: Waiting for data to be written (16 words)
Enum.name: WAITING

Enum.description: Digest is ready. Application may read it or may write more data.
Enum.name: READY

Enum.description: An error occurred since last cleared (written 1 to clear).
Enum.name: ERROR

Enum.description: No Key is needed and writes will not be treated as Key
Enum.name: NOT_NEED

Enum.description: Key is needed and INDATA/ALIAS will be accepted as Key. Will also set WAITING.
Enum.name: NEED

Enum.description: No IV/Nonce is needed, either because written already or because not needed.
Enum.name: NOT_NEED

Enum.description: IV/Nonce is needed and INDATA/ALIAS will be accepted as IV/Nonce. Will also set WAITING.
Enum.name: NEED

BitField.description: Interrupt When Waiting for Data Input
BitField.name: WAITING

Enum.description: Interrupt not enabled when Digest is ready
Enum.name: NO_INTERRUPT

Enum.description: Interrupt is enabled when Digest is ready. Interrupt cleared by writing more data, starting a new Hash, or disabling (done).
Enum.name: INTERRUPT

Enum.description: Interrupt is enabled on Error (until cleared).
Enum.name: INTERRUPT

Enum.description: Mastering is not used and the normal DMA or Interrupt based model is used with INDATA.
Enum.name: NOT_USED

Enum.description: Mastering is enabled and DMA and INDATA should not be used.
Enum.name: ENABLED

Enum.description: CTR mode (see details on IV/nonce). See also AESCTRPOS.
Enum.name: CTR

Enum.description: User key provided in normal way
Enum.name: NORMAL_WAY

Enum.description: Secret key provided in hidden way by HW
Enum.name: HIDDEN_WAY

Enum.description: 32 bits of the IV/ctr are used (from 127:96)
Enum.name: BITS_32

Enum.description: 64 bits of the IV/ctr are used (from 127:64)
Enum.name: BITS_64

Enum.description: 96 bits of the IV/ctr are used (from 127:32)
Enum.name: BITS_96

Enum.description: All 128 bits of the IV/ctr are used
Enum.name: BIT_128

BitField.description: Reads 1 if 2 x 512 bit buffers, 0 if only 1 x 512 bit
BitField.name: DUAL

BitField.description: Reads 1 if AHB Master is enabled
BitField.name: AHB

BitField.description: Reads 1 if AES 192 and 256 also included
BitField.name: AESKEY

BitField.description: Reads 1 if AES Secret key is available
BitField.name: SECRET

Enum.description: Unlocks, so block is open to all. But, AHB Master will only issue non-secure requests.
Enum.name: UNLOCK

Enum.name: LOCK

BitField.description: Must write 0xA75 to change lock state. A75:Pattern needed to change bits 1:0
BitField.name: PATTERN

Register.description: Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register
Register.name: AIRCR

BitField.description: Reserved for Debug use. This bit reads as 0. When writing to the register you must write 0 to this bit, otherwise behavior is UNPREDICTABLE. This bit is not banked between Security states.
BitField.name: VECTCLRACTIVE

BitField.description: System reset request. This bit allows software or a debugger to request a system reset. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW if SYSRESETREQS is 0. When SYSRESETREQS is set to 1, from Non-secure state this bit acts as RAZ/WI.
BitField.name: SYSRESETREQ

Enum.description: Do not request a system reset.
Enum.name: NO_REQUEST

BitField.description: System reset request, Secure state only. The value of this bit defines whether the SYSRESETREQ bit is functional for Non-secure use. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure State and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.
BitField.name: SYSRESETREQS

Enum.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is available to both Security states.
Enum.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE

Enum.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is only available to Secure state.
Enum.name: SECURE_ONLY

BitField.description: Interrupt priority grouping field. This field determines the split of group priority from subpriority. This bit is banked between Security states
BitField.name: PRIGROUP

BitField.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI Non-secure enable. The value of this bit defines whether BusFault and NMI exceptions are Non-secure, and whether exceptions target the Non-secure HardFault exception. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure-state and RO from Non-secure state.
BitField.name: BFHFNMINS

Enum.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI are Secure.
Enum.name: SECURE

Enum.description: BusFault and NMI are Non-secure and exceptions can target Non-secure HardFault.
Enum.name: NON_SECURE

BitField.description: Prioritize Secure exceptions. The value of this bit defines whether Secure exception priority boosting is enabled. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure state and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.
BitField.name: PRIS

Enum.description: Priority ranges of Secure and Non-secure exceptions are identical
Enum.name: SAME_PRIORITY

BitField.description: Data endianness bit. This bit is not banked between Security states.
BitField.name: ENDIANNESS

BitField.description: Register key: Reads as 0xFA05. On writes, write 0x5FA to VECTKEY, otherwise the write is ignored. This Field is not banked between Security states.
BitField.name: VECTKEY

Register.description: The SCR controls features of entry to and exit from low-power state.
Register.name: SCR

BitField.description: Indicates sleep-on-exit when returning from Handler mode to Thread mode. Setting this bit to 1 enables an interrupt driven application to avoid returning to an empty main application. This bit is banked between Security states.
BitField.name: SLEEPONEXIT

Enum.description: Do not sleep when returning to Thread mode.
Enum.name: NOT_SLEEP

Enum.description: Enter sleep, or deep sleep, on return from an ISR
Enum.name: SLEEP

BitField.description: Controls whether the processor uses sleep or deep sleep as its low-power mode. This bit is not banked between Security states.
BitField.name: SLEEPDEEP

BitField.description: Controls whether the SLEEPDEEP bit is only accessible from the Secure state. This bit in only accessible from the Secure state, and behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Nonsecure state. This bit is not banked between Security states.
BitField.name: SLEEPDEEPS

Enum.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit is accessible from both Security states.
Enum.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE

Enum.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Non-secure state.
Enum.name: SECURE_ONLY

BitField.description: Send Event on Pending bit. When an event or interrupt enters pending state, the event signal wakes up the processor from WFE. If the processor is not waiting for an event, the event is registered and affects the next WFE. The processor also wakes up on execution of an SEV instruction or an external event. This bit is banked between Security states.
BitField.name: SEVONPEND

Enum.description: Only enabled interrupts or events can wakeup the processor, disabled interrupts are excluded.
Enum.name: EXCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS

Enum.description: Enabled events and all interrupts, including disabled interrupts, can wakeup the processor
Enum.name: INCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
